# help showsys
showsys - Show system information.

SYNTAX
    showsys [options]

DESCRIPTION
    The showsys command displays storage system properties such as the system
    name, serial number, and system capacity information.

AUTHORITY
    Any role in the system

OPTIONS
    -block
        Displays system capacity information by only looking at block-based
        virtual volumes (that is, excluding fileservice VVs). This option
        can only be issued with -detailspace, -domainspace, -space or -vvspace.

    -d
        Specifies that more detailed information about the system is displayed.

    -desc
        Displays the system descriptor properties.

    -devtype {SSD|QLC}
        Displays the system capacity information where the disks must have a
        device type string matching the specified device type; either Triple
        Layer Cell Solid State Drive (SSD) or Quad Layer Cell (QLC). This
        option can only be issued with -detailspace, -domainspace, -space or
        -vvspace.

    -detailspace
        Displays the system capacity information in MiB in more detail than
        -space.

    -domainspace
        Displays the system capacity information broken down by domain in MiB.

    -fileservice
        Displays system capacity information by only looking at fileservice-
        related virtual volumes (that is, excluding block-based VVs). This
        option can only be issued with -detailspace, -domainspace, -space or
        -vvspace.

    -param
        Specifies that the system parameters are displayed.

    -space
        Displays the system capacity information in MiB.

    -syslogprofile
        Specifies that the Remote syslog configuration files are displayed.

    -vvspace
        Displays the system capacity information in MiB with an emphasis on
        VVs.

SPECIFIERS
    None.

NOTES
    See setsys command for information on setting the threshold parameters
    indicated by the Value column in the output for showsys -param.

    In the output for showsys -param, "from configured settings" indicates that
    the system parameters displayed have been successfully read from the
    Persistent Repository (PR). If the PR is not available (most likely because
    of problems with the admin volume), the output reads "from default settings"
    and the values displayed would indicate the system defaults. When "from
    default settings" is displayed, system parameters cannot be updated.

    If the VVRetentionTimeMax is 0, then the volume retention time in the system
    is disabled.

    For the system capacity information, there might be some overlaps among
    Volumes, System, and Failed Capacities.

EXAMPLES
    The following example displays the system descriptor properties of a
    storage system:

        cli% showsys -desc
        ------------System s36------------
        System Name  :  s36
        Location     :  Your Facility Address
        Owner        :  Your Company Name
        Contact      :  Joe Admin
        Comment      :  Your Notes

    The following example displays more detailed (-d option) information about
    the same storage server:

        cli% showsys -d
